financing.summary: Private, founder-led and self-described 'builder-owned' Florida builder (554 to 555 closings in 2025) with no public debt, no SEC filings and no disclosed lender, credit facility, land banker or outside capital partner. It is a conventional for-sale builder, but its land model is unusual: most homes go up one at a time on scattered infill lots it buys from individual owners and the MLS in pre-platted communities (Cape Coral, Lehigh Acres, Port Charlotte, Palm Bay, Citrus Springs, Marion Oaks), plus a build-on-your-lot programme, which needs little land capital and is a poor fit for a classic land-bank structure. The opening for a land banker is the newer community business: it took finished homesites in West Port (111 lots, 2022) and Babcock Ranch (291 homes, 2023), and in September 2026 was named one of five builders in Barron Collier's 2,000-home Brightshore in Naples, alongside Pulte, Toll, Taylor Morrison and M/I. So it is a plausible but small land-banking customer, most likely for bulk finished-lot takedowns in master plans; how it funds those today is not public.
financing.land_strategy: Asset-light by design rather than by option: the CEO has said the company enters markets where there is a single ('spot') lot opportunity because it carries much less risk, and the company's current land-acquisition job posting describes sourcing scattered, spot and infill lots from the MLS. It also solicits land sellers directly ('one or one-thousand lots') and takes finished homesites from master developers (West Port, Babcock Ranch, Brightshore). No owned/optioned split or stated target is published.

lots.source_title: Christopher Alan Homes 'Sell Your Land' page
lots.note: No lot counts are published (private company). The only lot-level numbers in public sources are per-community: 111 homesites in the first phase of The Hammocks at West Port (2022) and 291 homes at Creekside Run in Babcock Ranch (2023). The Brightshore allocation is not disclosed.

land_banking.description: Master developer of Brightshore (about 680 acres, roughly 2,000 homes, Immokalee Road, Naples). Christopher Alan Homes is one of five builders selected, with Toll Brothers, Taylor Morrison, Pulte and M/I Homes; its neighbourhood is marketed as Horizon at Brightshore. The developer says it will soon turn homesites over to builders, with models expected by summer 2027.
land_banking.source_title: Barron Collier Companies Names Five Homebuilders at Brightshore (developer press release)
land_banking.note: This is a finished-lot purchase relationship with a developer, not a land-bank facility. Lot count, price and takedown terms for Christopher Alan Homes are not disclosed (M/I Homes separately disclosed 526 lots there). The builder's own site confirms the community as 'coming soon': https://christopheralanhomes.com/horizon-at-brightshore/. Largest and most recent community commitment found; the most likely place a lot-option financier would be useful.

land_banking.counterparty: Babcock Ranch (master-planned community; developer not named in the source)
land_banking.description: Creekside Run, the builder's first neighbourhood in Babcock Ranch: 291 single-family homes on about 100 acres in the Midtown phase, announced February 2023 with sales launched later that year.
land_banking.source_title: Christopher Alan Homes announces Creekside Run neighborhood in Babcock Ranch (company release carried by Southwest Florida Business Today)
land_banking.note: Not a land-bank facility. How the land was bought or financed is not disclosed. Babcock Ranch is not among the locations on the builder's site as of November 2026 and a June 2026 company release describes the business as building on individual homesites, so this position may be sold out, sold or wound down; current status unconfirmed.

land_banking.counterparty: West Port, Port Charlotte (master-planned community; developer not named in the source)
land_banking.description: Hammock Village / The Hammocks at West Port: 111 homesites announced May 2022; a second phase was being planned as of January 2024.
land_banking.source_title: Christopher Alan Homes Announces Expansion into New Home Community (company release carried by Southwest Florida Business Today)
land_banking.note: Not a land-bank facility; terms not disclosed. Second-phase reference is from the company's January 2024 release (https://swfloridabusinesstoday.com/christopher-alan-homes-experienced-tremendous-growth-in-2023-looking-ahead-to-2024/). Not listed on the builder's site as of November 2026; current status unconfirmed.

key_metrics.source_title: Strategy shift pays off for locally based homebuilder (Business Observer, 2023-05-19)

gaps: Credit facility, construction lenders, land loans: not publicly disclosed (private company, no SEC filings, no lender named in any press item opened).
Land banker, lot-option partner or outside capital partner: none found in public sources; the company calls itself 'builder-owned'.
Owned versus optioned lots, total lots controlled, years of supply: not publicly disclosed.
Balance sheet (debt, cash, liquidity, leverage) and credit ratings: not publicly disclosed; key_metrics is empty for that reason.

Revenue: the company gave Business Observer $80.5M (2020), $133.6M (2021) and $141.98M (2022), and in January 2024 anticipated $203M for 2023; 2024 and 2025 revenue could not be confirmed because the Builder 100 pages on builderonline.com returned 403 (the orchestrator's roughly $180M lead for 2025 is unverified).

M&A 2025 to date: no acquisition, sale or merger involving Christopher Alan Homes found in the company site, Business Observer, Southwest Florida Business Today or the Barron Collier newsroom. Growth has been organic (LaBelle October 2025; Ocala / Marion Oaks October 2026; Brightshore September 2026; Spring Hill and Royal Highlands listed as coming soon).

Link to Domain Real Estate Partners, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon: none found. One combined search for the builder with 'land bank' / 'lot option' / lender terms returned nothing relevant; the shared web-search allowance then ran out, so name-by-name competitor queries were not run.
Brightshore lot count, price and takedown schedule for Christopher Alan Homes: not disclosed by the developer or the builder.
County mortgage records and Florida UCC filings (which would name lenders) were not searched; the Florida corporate registry (Sunbiz) returned 403.

Affiliates: an in-house title agency (CAH Title, in the same Fort Myers office park) and a preferred mortgage lender (Sunshine Lending) serve homebuyers; neither is a source of corporate or land financing as far as public sources show. The builder grew out of concrete-shell contractor JHS Builders (Business Observer, 2020); the current relationship between the two entities is not public.
